limitations: Every fixture in this suite is project-authored. The suite demonstrates boundary enforcement on KNOWN traps; it is not evidence of generality against unseen traps, because the party that must pass the controls also wrote them.

GC-04 substitutes a recorded FORMAL_ARTIFACT bound to the statement it actually proves for a real formal kernel. Running Lean on a weakened translation needs the sealed Phase 3B runtime and the ADR-0016 v5 image, which the offline check deliberately excludes.
GC-05 uses synthetic source spans and a synthetic imported statement. The benchmark paper arXiv:quant-ph/0201109 is metadata-only with no licensed local content.
GC-01 is one hand-built dossier. It makes the suite non-vacuous; it does not measure known-theorem coverage, which at any meaningful scale means mathlib or a literature corpus.
GC-09A tests the Section 18.2 plugin CONTRACT with a minimal second-domain fixture. Building an actual second domain plugin is out of scope.

No metric of the form 'catches X per cent of unseen traps' is computable from repository data. The release package's baseline_comparison counts enforced trust boundaries, which is not a generality rate and must not be read as one.
Novelty and significance are not assessed anywhere in this suite. External expert review is out-of-repo labour and is not substituted for.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 known theorems; Section 17.5 tier 1

probe.forbidden_outcome: The suite reports all controls passing while having proved nothing, because every control asserts non-admission and the system under test rejects everything.

limitations: One hand-built dossier, not a known-theorem corpus.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 false conjectures; Section 17.5 tier 2; Section 20 scenario C

parameters.target_statement: For all integers a and b, if a and b are even, then a + b is odd.

probe.forbidden_outcome: A false universal reaches proved or supported status, or any warrant kind at all is allowed to report it disproved.

limitations: The counterexample is recorded, not searched for. No counterexample search exists in this slice.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 false conjectures; Section 17.5 tier 5 numerical-to-exact

probe.forbidden_outcome: An exact nonoptimal fixed point of the JRF iteration is reported as convergence to the optimum, so the false universal convergence conjecture looks confirmed.

limitations: The case is carried inline. Appending it to fixtures/phase5/quantum-diagonal-v1.json would change that fixture's canonical hash, which the confirmatory protocol pins.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 missing-assumption traps; Section 17.5 tier 3

assumption_delta: the local target assumes a and b are even; the formalization omits that hypothesis

probe.forbidden_outcome: The target resolves as proved while a named hypothesis is missing, or the omission silently demotes the translated claim too, collapsing semantic custody and logical status into one axis.

limitations: The omitted hypothesis is named by the fixture, not detected. Nothing here discovers a missing assumption.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 semantic mistranslations; Section 17.5 tier 6; Section 20 scenario H

parameters.formal_statement: When a=0 and b=0, a+b is even.

probe.value: For all integers a and b, if a and b are even, then a + b is even.
probe.forbidden_outcome: A formal artifact that proves a weakened statement resolves the original target, so a mistranslation carries the target's warrant.

limitations: No formal kernel runs. The formal warrant is a recorded FORMAL_ARTIFACT whose verification record is bound to the statement hash it actually covers; Lean on a weakened translation needs the sealed Phase 3B runtime.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 inapplicable citations; Section 17.5 tier 7; Section 20 scenario I

probe.forbidden_outcome: A real but inapplicable source closes a literature_applicability obligation, so the proof step stops being an obligation without an applicability check.

limitations: The imported statement, its hypotheses, and the source span are synthetic. No licensed local content for a real inapplicable citation exists in this repository.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 cross-representation problems; Section 17.5 tier 4; Section 20 scenario D

probe.forbidden_outcome: A transformed result carries weight for the original claim across a representation map that is only partially verified.

limitations: One representation map over integer algebra. No real cross-representation corpus exists here.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 cross-representation problems; Section 20 scenario D

probe.forbidden_outcome: A transformed result carries weight for the original claim while its bridge obligation is still open.

probe.forbidden_outcome: Agreement between models produces proof status. The probe also shows the control discriminates on warrant kind rather than always answering supported.

limitations: No model is called. The MODEL_AGREEMENT warrant is recorded, which is the only offline form of this scenario.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 20 scenario B experimental overreach; ADR-0024 control finite_experiment_overreach

probe.forbidden_outcome: Finitely many verified inputs are reported as a universal proof of an unrestricted_universal claim.

limitations: The enforcement measured here is the warrant-kind branch in domain/policies.py. The explicit scope demotion at policies.py lines 127-131 is unreachable, so this control does not exercise it; see ADR-0034.

probe.value: For all integers k, 2k is even.
probe.forbidden_outcome: A helper lemma described as standard, whose statement is the unresolved target, closes the target obligation.

limitations: Detection is exact normalized-statement equality. A paraphrased restatement is not detected.

controls.blueprint_reference: TECHNICAL_BLUEPRINT.md Section 18.4 later domain plugins must pass the same core contract without changing core entity semantics

probe.forbidden_outcome: A second domain needs a new core entity type, a new enum member, or its own trust rule, or the same trust rules stop discriminating once the domain changes.

limitations: This is the contract, not a second domain. One minimal graph-theory dossier is not evidence of coverage in graph theory.
